newsitem.title: UK: Paper fuel trade leaves Euro physical market behind.
newsitem.headline: Paper fuel trade leaves Euro physical market behind.

text.p: Activity in European fuel oil markets was overshadowed by paper business on Monday as players watched crude futures soar to two month highs, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $87 fob a tonne early before tailing off to $86, $85 and $85.50.

When crude rallied later, paper markets followed but physical business was thin as dealers puzzled over the reasons for the IPE Brent and NYMEX crude rally. "The market is on edge today because no-one is quite sure how long this crude rally will last," said one. "We are a little unsure of direction and it is always quiet the first day after the weekend."
Cargo paper soared to $93/$94 flat across May, June and July but one percent physical prices trailed behind at a notional $89/$91 fob a tonne, with no business seen done in an under-supplied market.

The market rumoured three figure offer numbers into Italy, but that was not borne out by the potential Mediterranean buyers. However notional cif figures were judged to be around $100/$101 in the Med.
